title: Tom Kha Gai–Thai Coconut Chicken Soup
description: Tom Kha Gai is a classic Thai coconut chicken soup, loved for its creamy coconut broth infused with fragrant lemongrass, galangal, kaffir lime leaves, and balanced with savory, sour, sweet, and spicy flavors.

ingredients.title: Aromatics (do not eat—used for infusion)
items: Lemongrass (white part only) – 3 stalks, cut into 2-inch pieces & smashed
Kaffir lime leaves – 4–6, torn by hand

ingredients.title: Soup Base
items: Chicken stock (preferably homemade or low-sodium) – 4 cups (1 L)
Chicken thigh (skinless, boneless) – 300 g, sliced thinly against the grain
Oyster mushrooms or straw mushrooms – 200 g, halved
Thai bird’s eye chilies – 3–4, bruised (or to taste)
Thai fish sauce – 1 tbsp (or to taste)
Lime juice – 1 tbsp (or more, added at the end)
Palm sugar (or light brown sugar) – 1 tsp

ingredients.title: Garnish (optional but recommended)
items: Sliced red chili or chili oil

instruction.title: Step 1 – Infuse the Broth
steps: In a medium pot, bring chicken stock to a simmer.
Add lemongrass, galangal, and kaffir lime leaves.
Simmer gently (no boil) for 5–7 minutes to infuse the aromatics.

instruction.title: Step 2 – Add Chicken and Mushrooms
steps: Add the chicken, shallots, and mushrooms.
Simmer gently for 5–6 minutes or until chicken is cooked through.

instruction.title: Step 3 – Add Coconut Milk
steps: Pour in the coconut milk. Stir gently to avoid curdling.
Add bruised chilies, fish sauce, and palm sugar.
Let simmer for another 3–5 minutes. Do not boil after coconut milk is added—it can split.

instruction.title: Step 4 – Balance the Flavor
steps: Remove from heat. Taste the soup.
Adjust with lime juice, more fish sauce, or a touch more sugar depending on your preference:

instruction.title: Step 5 – Serve
steps: Ladle into bowls, avoiding the large lemongrass and galangal slices.
Garnish with cilantro, chili slices, and a lime wedge on the side.

servingSuggestions.title: Serving Suggestions
items: Serve hot as a starter or light meal.
Pair with steamed jasmine rice for a complete meal.
Garnish with fresh cilantro, chili slices, and lime wedges.

chefTips: Galangal is essential for “Tom Kha” — “kha” means galangal in Thai.
Never boil after coconut milk is added to prevent curdling.
Mushroom substitute: use button or enoki mushrooms if oyster/straw aren’t available.
For a vegetarian version, substitute chicken with tofu and use soy sauce instead of fish sauce.
Add a splash of nam prik pao (Thai chili jam) for a roasted depth, commonly used in some regional versions.
